proof:
The lower graph is convex, and the plane $x=0$ meets the interior of exactly those real fibers over the interior of the base cube. At the sampled proper sites the through-section has counting measure one, and at the remaining sampled sites the plane meets exactly the lower endpoint. The total at proper sites is $81$ with zero base moment. The supporting-site counts by first coordinate $-2,-1,0,1,2$ are $125,98,98,98,125$, since the three inner slices have $125-27=98$ supporting sites. With the stated fractions, summing those counts times the weights gives $73390/397$. Their first-coordinate moment is $2(125)(375/397)+98/2-(250+98)(22/397)=105547/397$. The proper weight adds $81$ to the total and zero to the moment. All other moments vanish by coordinate reflection. This proves the barycenter formula.

At the mark $(e_1,0)$ write the nearby cap as $x\le a\cdot(z-e_1)$. At a differentiability parameter sufficiently near zero, the gradient is $\sum_{z\in I}(z-e_1)+\sum_{z\in J:\,a\cdot(z-e_1)>0}(z-e_1)$, by the clipped interval lengths. Take the rays in the directions $a_\pm=(1,\pm (1,10,100)/1000)$ and their negatives. In the first two rays the signs are positive throughout $z_1=2$, negative throughout $z_1\le0$, and complementary in the slice $z_1=1$. Indeed the absolute perturbation is at most $222/1000$, and at a supporting site in the slice the remaining coordinate vector is nonzero and its highest nonzero base-ten digit dominates all lower ones. Thus all four rays consist near zero of actual differentiability parameters. Averaging the first two gradients yields optional trace one on $z_1=2$, one half on $z_1=1$, and zero on $z_1\le0$. The negative rays yield the complementary array. Including proper weights, their averaged first gradients are $125-81=44$ and $-669-81=-750$ and the other coordinates vanish by reflection. Weighting the two averages by $375/397$ and $22/397$ gives zero and exactly the prescribed trace fractions. Reflections and permutations carry the construction to each other vertex mark. Since the arrays have equal total weight, their convex combinations give exactly the corresponding convex combinations of their barycenters.

For the strict local assertion subtract the zero first-order term for these fractions $\theta_z$. The actual excess mass near $a=0$ is $\sum_{z\in J}[(a\cdot(z-e_1))_+-\theta_z a\cdot(z-e_1)]$: the proper terms were linear and have been canceled using the barycenter. Each summand is at least $(22/397)|a\cdot(z-e_1)|$. The vectors $z-e_1$ for $z\in J$ span $\mathbb R^4$ because the supporting sites include all vertices of the base cube. The excess is therefore positive for $a\ne0$.

In the product, each section is the unit-volume continuous cube in the new coordinates $w$, so its added first moments vanish by symmetry. The same four rays with $w$-coefficient zero are actual differentiability parameters for all normal parameters near those rays' nonzero points: the supporting signs are strict on the compact cube at each such point, and the proper thresholds are interior there. Thus the same limit combination applies. For a sufficiently small through-mark perturbation $x\le a\cdot(z-e_1)+b\cdot w$, the same excess identity holds integrated over the cube, using its zero $w$ moment. It is bounded below by $22/397$ times the sum of integrals of $|a\cdot(z-e_1)+b\cdot w|$ over the cube for $z\in J$. If that sum vanishes, each affine integrand vanishes everywhere by continuity and the cube's interior, forcing $b=0$ and then $a=0$ by spanning. This proves the local assertion in all continuous dimensions stated.

statement:
On the body $C_T=\{(z,x):z\in[-2,2]^4,\ \lVert z\rVert_\infty-2\le x\le T\}$, $T\ge1$, with four integer coordinates and one continuous coordinate, take the downward cap $x\le0$. On its section the $81$ proper sampled sites in $I=\{-1,0,1\}^4$ have compulsory counting weight one. The $544$ lower supporting sites $J=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}^4\setminus I$ have optional full weight one. Assign to the supporting sites of $z_1=2,\ z_1=1,\ z_1\le0$ the trace fractions $375/397,\ 1/2,\ 22/397$, respectively. These traces arise from a convex combination, with coefficients $375/794,375/794,11/397,11/397$, of four actual nearby cap-gradient limits at the mark $(e_1,0)$. Their supporting weight is $73390/397$ and the total weight and first-coordinate moment are both $105547/397$, so the effective section barycenter is $(e_1,0)$. Reflections and permutations give the distinct same-parity pair $(\pm e_1,0)$ and all $(\pm e_i,0)$. Convex combinations of the equal-weight trace arrays give all effective section barycenters in their crosspolytope.

At each vertex mark the cap is a strict local minimum over nonvertical through-point directions. For every $d\ge2$ the product with $[-1/2,1/2]^{d-1}$ has the corresponding trace certificates and the same strict local minimum at the lifted vertex marks over all nonvertical through-point directions.
title: Actual cap-gradient limits with same-parity proper section barycenters
